assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a new boson consistent with the Standard Model Higgs is a clear, concrete discovery: it completed the electroweak sector, confirmed the symmetry-breaking mechanism and has been followed by a decade of coupling measurements. Of the candidates, it is the one where the discovery itself is most unambiguous.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognised the theoretical prediction; the experimental discovery was made by two large collaborations. Credit to the founding leaders and proponents of the detectors (ATLAS: Jenni, with Della Negra as early ATLAS/CMS leader; CMS: Virdee, Della Negra) is defensible but necessarily stands in for thousands of contributors, and the accelerator/LHC side is not represented in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: independent confirmation by two experiments, Tevatron hints, and thirteen years of follow-up with properties stable. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit is an inherently imperfect fit with the three-person limit and the choice of individuals is contestable.
Whether the committee wants to honour leadership roles versus the analysis teams that made the observation is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials: a theoretical flat-band prediction followed by experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in a simple, tunable system. Originality and downstream impact (a whole field of twistronics, fractional Chern insulators) are very high.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the experimental discovery of correlated states and superconductivity. The pairing of one theorist and one experimentalist is fairly clean, though a third name could be Bistritzer; Cao and others in the experimental team and earlier theorists (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) are not in the credited set.
assessment.maturity: Roughly eight years from the 2018 experiments; many groups reproduced the phenomena, and the interpretation of superconductivity is still debated, but the core discovery is robust.
uncertainties: Priority of the earlier theoretical work on twisted bilayer band flattening is not represented in the credited names.
Is MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero enough, or does the allocation of credit to Bistritzer matter?

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP delivered precision measurement of the CMB anisotropies, fixing the age, geometry and composition of the Universe and establishing the standard Lambda-CDM model. It is a cornerstone discovery of cosmology, extending the work already honoured in 2006 (COBE) and 2019.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission as PI, Page was central to instrument design and Spergel to the cosmological analysis and interpretation. The three-way split is reasonable, though Wilkinson and others in the team also had major roles.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed by Planck and ground-based experiments; recognition is late but not premature. The risk is that the committee views Planck and WMAP as an incremental refinement of COBE.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees the WMAP advance as sufficiently distinct from COBE and from the 2019 cosmology prize.
Planck's independent contribution complicates a WMAP-only award.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar-timing evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background opens a new window on supermassive black-hole binaries or early-universe physics. It is a major result in gravitational physics and astrophysics.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA and IPTA; McLaughlin (NANOGrav), Kramer (EPTA) and Manchester (PPTA) are plausible regional representatives, but the founding ideas (Hellings-Downs, Detweiler, Sazhin) and the pulsar discoverers lie elsewhere.
assessment.maturity: Premature: the 2023 evidence is at roughly 3-4 sigma with the Hellings-Downs signature, and the source (binaries versus new physics) is unresolved. Timing arrays have not yet made a clean individual detection.
uncertainties: Statistical significance below the conventional discovery threshold.
Source of the signal is unidentified.
Allocation among four collaborations is contentious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Gauge/gravity duality is among the deepest conceptual advances in theoretical physics, reshaping quantum gravity, black-hole physics, QCD-like strongly coupled systems and condensed matter. Its originality and reach are exceptional, but the Nobel Prize in Physics weighs empirical foundation and I note the correspondence is not tested in nature.
assessment.attribution: Maldacena's 1997 conjecture is the decisive step; Gubser-Klebanov-Polyakov and Witten supplied the dictionary. The trio is the natural configuration, though Polyakov's role is partly in earlier string/gauge ideas.
assessment.maturity: Mathematically very robust and heavily cross-checked (integrability, localisation), but without direct experimental confirmation of the duality in a real physical system. Timing could be argued either way.
uncertainties: No direct empirical test; the committee's long-standing preference for confirmed discoveries applies.
Applicability to real QCD or condensed-matter systems is only approximate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory and observation of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect established a new class of quantum matter with robust edge states, with a broad impact across condensed matter. Experimental realisations are clear and the field is mature.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) made the decisive theoretical prediction, Molenkamp's group the first experimental observation in HgTe, and Xue the quantum anomalous Hall realisation. This candidate mixes distinct discoveries, and the Mele and Zhang/Bernevig contributions, central to the story, are not in this entry's credited names.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed; recognition is timely though the 2016 topological prize already covered earlier topological phases.
uncertainties: Compound discovery (QSH versus QAH) with different recognition needs.
Absence of Mele, who shared the decisive theory, from the credited names for this entry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation resolved the horizon and flatness problems and, via quantum fluctuations (Mukhanov), explained the origin of cosmic structure; it underpins modern cosmology. As a theorist in cosmology I regard it as conceptually essential.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed the scenario, Linde the new/chaotic inflation fixing the graceful exit, Mukhanov the fluctuation spectrum. Starobinsky's earlier model is not among the credited names, so the fairness of this configuration is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Predictions of a nearly scale-invariant spectrum are supported, but primordial gravitational waves have not been detected and alternatives are not excluded, so the confirmation is only partial; recognition is arguably premature.
uncertainties: No decisive observational discrimination from alternatives.
Starobinsky's priority is excluded from the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction made scalable quantum computation conceivable via fault tolerance, and now guides experiments that reach below-threshold logical error rates. The conceptual originality is high and its role in the field is foundational.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane independently constructed the first codes; Kitaev introduced topological codes and anyonic ideas. Gottesman, Calderbank, Knill and Laflamme and others made important contributions that are not in the credited names, so the configuration is only approximately complete.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations of logical-qubit improvement are recent (2023-25), so the implementation is still early, although the theory is well established; timing is borderline.
uncertainties: Whether the committee waits for a demonstrated scalable fault-tolerant machine.
Credit boundaries with Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme are blurry.
